spots.parkroyal: A clean, spacious North Shore shopping centre with indoor and outdoor sections, a food court and a great variety of shops, good for a rainy-day outing.
spots.albertdyckpark: A park around a man-made lake with a trail, a small beach, a boat ramp, a picnic area and a dock. It's great for paddling, and the lake is tested for water quality, so check before swimming. Reviewers don't recommend it for kids under 5.
spots.kirkstoneskatepark: A recently resurfaced, very smooth skatepark with shade trees and green space. It can get crowded quickly, and the big features are better for older kids.
spots.londonfarm: A heritage farmhouse and garden in Steveston with welcoming volunteers and fascinating history. You can book a light afternoon tea with scones, and the dyke trail is next door.
spots.keswickpark: A hilly park with a toddler-to-elementary playground, a small spray park, swings, a basketball court, a jogging track and washrooms. Street parking can be tight.
spots.jonespark: A hidden neighbourhood park with a pirate-ship play area, an old-school merry-go-round, a giant snail and a sandpit, mostly in the shade. It has washrooms, a drinking fountain, a big field and outdoor fitness equipment.
spots.godwinfarmbiodiversitypr: A peaceful 1.3 km loop past a pond, towering redwoods, a meadow and an orchard. It's flat, easy and takes about 30 minutes, with parking and a washroom on the trail.
spots.waderoadpark: A clean, well-kept park with a large playground, swings, slides, a soccer field and washrooms, and plenty of parking. The playground could use an upgrade.
spots.brydonlagoon: A small lake with an easy walking loop and hundreds of ducks, wood ducks, geese, turtles and loons. Blackberries and salmonberries in season, and it takes a little effort to find.
spots.bluemountainspraypark: A well-loved spray park with different levels, a wading pool, a big playground, a field, lots of shade and seating, a concession stand and washrooms nearby, with lots of parking.
spots.mapleridgemuseumcommunit: A small, quaint museum on Maple Ridge history and the local Japanese community, with a beautiful model train set and diorama in the basement. Friendly hosts, and it's a quick visit.
spots.oldschoolhousepark: A big park with a nice playground, a huge covered picnic area, a sandbox, courts, outdoor exercise equipment and a large field, surrounded by shops. Best for little kids.
spots.greendaleacreschilliwack: A fun family farm with a corn maze, sunflower maze, u-pick flowers, roasted corn, a train ride, tractor cart rides, face painting and farm animals. Parents say there's an endless list of kids' activities, including an indoor barn with a corn sandpit. Plan 5 hours or more.
spots.evergreenparkplayground: A quiet, mostly shaded park with a good-size playground with tires, washrooms, a large field and basketball and tennis courts. Great for a family picnic.
spots.tantaluspark: A quiet, shaded field with a small playground with baby swings, climbing structures, a digger and sand. There's no bathroom or parking, and it's usually deserted.
spots.willbandcreekpark: A beautiful flat trail beside a creek, with a small lake with islands, curved bridges, a lookout and lots of wildlife. There are few shaded areas on hot days, and a porta potty is at the start.
spots.laserdomeplus: A compact laser tag arena with three activities and friendly, fun staff who run stress-free kids' birthday parties with pizza. Parents find it fairly priced.
spots.jollybubblerichmond: A bright, very clean indoor play zone with over 10,000 sq. ft., themed play areas and a separate area for little ones. Staff are friendly, and birthday parties are well organized.
spots.poplarpark: A recently reopened park with new structures for tots and bigger kids, baby swings, slides, a big grassy area, shade and a water fountain. No washrooms.
spots.princeedwardpark: A clean, kid-friendly park with a spray park, a big playground that suits toddlers to older kids, a large field and mountain views. Washrooms depend on the season.
spots.hazelnutmeadowscommunity: A park with two playgrounds, picnic tables and short forest trails where rabbits show up. Families call it clean and lovely.
spots.mackiepark: A park with a playground, turf and grass soccer and football fields, a baseball diamond, short forest trails and North Delta's only fenced off-leash dog park.
spots.noelboothcommunitypark: A big park with bike-friendly trails, a pond, turf soccer and softball fields and a frisbee golf area. A calm, friendly spot to walk.
spots.sheffieldpark: A newer park with a rubber-floored playground, a spray park with trap doors, a sandbox, a basketball court, a skating court, clean washrooms and great views from the top of the slide. It's short on shade.
spots.horsemanspark: A calm green area on the Alouette River, a favourite for a picnic after tubing, wading in the creek and walking the trails.
spots.sappertonlandingpark: A riverfront strip with walkways, a family picnic gazebo and views of trains and the SkyTrain that little ones enjoy. Street parking on Cumberland St.
spots.barberpark: A tucked-away neighbourhood park with separate play areas for ages 2 to 5 and 5 to 12, a take-a-book leave-a-book kiosk, shade, a big field and a basketball hoop. Parking costs $7 during river floating season.
spots.portcoquitlamcommunityce: A big multi-sport community centre with a pool, rink, gym, the Terry Fox Library and a spray park. Many programs, great instructors and a huge underground parking garage.
spots.icearenawestvancouver: A decent-size rink inside the West Vancouver community centre complex, with skating and hockey lessons, rentals included in private lessons and underground parking.
spots.matsquitrailregionalpark: A wide, flat, well-kept trail along the Fraser River under the Mission Bridge, great for families with strollers and bikes. There are picnic tables, many with fire pits.
spots.princesspark: A park with a fenced playground, swings, slides and climbing structures, public washrooms, tennis courts, forested trails and creeks. Off-leash dog areas make it a meeting place, and there's ample parking.
spots.olympicexperienceatrichm: An interactive museum at the Richmond Olympic Oval with race simulators, virtual skiing and hands-on exhibits that kids love. Everything is new and clean.
spots.erniewinchpark: A park with a school-bus play structure that kids love, a younger kids' area, a jungle gym, a small spray park, tennis courts and shade trees. Street parking only.
spots.tisdallpark: A spacious park with a big field with two baseball diamonds, a duck pond, outdoor exercise equipment and several sections of play area with swings, a jungle gym, rope climbing and slides.
spots.goldstonepark: A clean park with a kids' playground, a water park, a soccer field, basketball and tennis courts, a jogging track, clean washrooms and free parking, close to the YMCA. A favourite for families.
spots.brunswickpoint: A flat, stroller-friendly gravel trail along the shore and dyke, with ocean, farmland and mountain views and lots of birds. There's a new parking lot but no restrooms, and pets stay on leash.
spots.portagepark: A park on the Nicomekl trail with top-condition playground equipment, paved paths, trails through grass and streams and named trees. Geocaches too, but the trail down has a steep gravel slope.
spots.normstaffpark: A quiet park with tall slides and a high play structure best for ages 4 and 5 and up, a little water park and lots to climb. No parking, so find a spot in the neighbourhood.
spots.fletcherpark: A clean, quiet park with two sizes of playground, monkey bars, a tire swing, a large grass area for ball games and a good play mix for ages 3 and up.
spots.loottoycompany: A New West shop making bath bombs with a toy inside, made in house with safe, gentle ingredients. Kids get excited about bath time, and the owners are kind and explain each product.
spots.qoqolempark: A short, family-friendly hike on a well-maintained gravel path, with benches, picnic tables, washrooms at the start and top and a view over the Vedder River and valley. Some steep sections, less than 5 km round trip.
spots.junglejacs: A big jungle-themed indoor play centre with climbing, slides, trampolines and bumper cars (extra fee) that suits a 4-year-old and a 12-year-old alike. Bring grippy socks, and food isn't allowed in. Great birthday parties.
spots.fishtrapcreekpark: A quiet trail around a small lake with bridges, ducks and geese, easy enough for anyone. There's parking and outhouses at Gardner Park and a playground on the side.
spots.delbrookpark: A neighbourhood park with a dragon-themed play feature that kids love, a playground with a good mix of sun and shade, soccer fields and tennis courts with public restrooms.
spots.paulikneighbourhoodpark: A small garden park that people call the fairy park, with fairy gardens, flower beds, a pavilion, a mini kids' playground and picnic tables. There are no public bathrooms.
spots.taylorpark: A park with a small bike park for younger kids, a playground with a huge sand area, a basketball court, trails and gardens, plus an off-leash dog park. No public washroom nearby.
spots.bakerviewpark: A clean park with a sand pit with diggers, a big tree for kids to climb, picnic tables, washrooms, big parking and paved accessible walkways. A go-to for little kids in South Surrey.
spots.sunburypark: A fenced play area for kids 5 and under with big shady trees, a baseball field, a basketball hoop, short trails and a refurbished hall.
spots.rotarychildrensplaygroun: A well-maintained playground with a rope climbing structure, swings, two fake horses, a wading pool, a spray park, covered picnic tables, accessible washrooms and free street parking. Great for birthday gatherings.
spots.hollypark2: A cute little playground for preschoolers at the end of a quiet road, with newly replaced equipment (2022), a small climbing wall, shade and a picnic table. Careful with toddlers on the shorter slide edge.
spots.queensboroughcommunityce: A cosy community centre with a library, a gym, programs and birthday parties, plus a nice water park and a skate park across the street. Free parking.
spots.terryfoxlibrary: A library in the Port Coquitlam community centre with a children's section, lots of kids' programs, friendly staff and a cafe with big cookies. Good on rainy Saturdays.
spots.batemanpark: A big park with a kids' playground, picnic spots, baseball and soccer fields, a creek trail and a fenced off-leash dog area, connected to Stoney Creek Park. Park and washrooms are very clean.
spots.lynnmouthpark: A park by the creek with an amazing playground, lots of room to play, bike and run, a picnic area, a restroom and a fenced dog park. Good for swimming and walking.
spots.gulfofgeorgiacannerynati: A history museum with interactive activities for kids and adults, an ocean- and fish-themed play area, old canning machinery and a harbour view. You can step out for fish and chips and come back in with your receipt.
spots.burnabyheightspark: A hilltop park with great North Shore mountain views, a good-size playground, tennis, basketball, a floor hockey court, soccer fields, clean washrooms and a fenced dog park.
spots.riverfrontpark: A Fraser River park with a great kids' playground with water fixtures, sand and a huge climbing and slide area, plus walking and biking trails and picnic tables.
spots.ermastephensonpark: A community park with a basic spray park, a small free library with books, ample picnic tables and shade, a soccer and baseball field and a well-maintained washroom. The pavement is hot on bare feet.
spots.gundersonpark: A neighbourhood park with two baseball diamonds, a lacrosse box, a decent playground, a few frisbee golf holes, green space and working bathrooms. Street parking when it's busy.
spots.fortlangleypark: A quiet, shady park with a playground, a spray park, picnic tables, washrooms and a covered eating area (bring your own table and seats). It's a short walk to food and drinks, with trains passing by.
spots.hoycreekhatchery: A small salmon hatchery in the Hoy Creek trails, educational for kids, especially when the fish are returning. Parking is limited, and watch for black bears and stay on the bridges.
spots.volkerpark: A large, quiet park with two playgrounds for ages 2 to 5, a paved bike path, a big grassy area great for kites and mountain views. No bathroom, and street parking only.
spots.newwestminsterpubliclibr: A clean, spacious, recently renovated library with friendly staff, an upper floor with desks, lots of activities and a good kids' section. A parent says their 8-year-old learned to read there.
spots.philippsonfamilypark: A local playground with its own water park, great slides, a fake-grass hill the kids roll down without getting dirty, nice views and well-kept lawns.
spots.silverbrookfarm: A farm with a petting zoo, a fishing pond where kids easily catch fish, BBQ shelters and room for birthdays. Bring seasoning and utensils, and staff are friendly.
spots.loutetpark: A popular North Shore park with grass fields, a playground for small kids, a bike park, forest trails and a garden farm next door. Washrooms are at the south end.
spots.kinneeparkplayground: A community park with beautiful new play structures, a zip line, swings, features for toddlers and older kids, a sizeable field, a water fountain and a pond with ducks. It's close to the SkyTrain, with only a few benches.
spots.fraserriverpark: A flat, clean waterfront park with gravel trails, boardwalks, a little beach and big open spaces for games. Good for kids, with parking and bathrooms at the east lot.
spots.kwantlenoutdoorpool: A free outdoor pool with a playground nearby, a basketball and soccer ball bin, clear water and lifeguards. It has two-hour swim sessions so kids and adults can both enjoy it.
spots.tsawwassencausewaybeach: A pebbly beach with sunset views, eagles and kayakers, with parking right by the water and porta potties. The road in is bumpy, and it's not for swimming.
spots.daleballpassivepark: A cute little walking loop with a disc golf course, a picnic area, a bathroom and a parking lot. Friendly regulars help newcomers.
spots.summitcommunitycentre: A clean, light community centre with kids' programs, warm, inclusive staff, drop-in programs, public restrooms and free parking.
spots.cliffpark: A short, scenic loop to a waterfall with a children's park at the start. It's about half an hour, with stairs that make it tricky for strollers, though parents do push them. It becomes a winter wonderland in snow.
spots.tamesew: A modern, beautifully designed city aquatic centre with warm, comfortable pools that families love. The change rooms get busy.
spots.centralcommunitypark: A small, level community park with mature shade trees, lovely gardens, bench seating, a great playground, a splash park and nearby restrooms.
spots.eaglemountainpark: A well-equipped playground suitable for all ages, a field with a walking track, fenced tennis and basketball courts, a portable washroom and killer views of Mount Baker and Sumas Prairie.
spots.hunterpark: A flat, easy trail with a big pond with ducks, herons and turtles, creeks and sometimes local horses. There are no amenities, and the pond has been used for skating.
spots.larrybergflightpathpark: A unique plane-watching park next to YVR with paper-airplane benches, miniature runways, a globe, a large grassy area and cherry blossoms. Kids who love planes adore it, with dedicated parking.
spots.avondalepark: A quiet, clean park with a midsized children's playground, a seesaw, a big open field, a few benches and a water fountain.
spots.connaughtpark: A Kitsilano park with a splash water park (bring extra clothes), a playground, shady benches and a community centre, with free parking. The farmers market sets up in the parking lot on Sundays.
spots.southsurreyindoorpool: A friendly indoor pool with great instructors for children, two saunas, a small tot pool, a medium pool and lift chairs for accessibility. It's closed in the middle of the day, 12 to 3.
spots.wellingtonpointpark: A small park with a new pier with views of the Fraser River, picnic tables on lawns, a boat launch and pit washrooms. Kids and adults can fish from the sturdy pier.
spots.brookswoodpark: A park with a splash pad (cold water), playground, baby swings, drinking water, washrooms and a wooded area behind the playground where kids collect branches for forts and a creek.
spots.albionpark: A new playground with four distinct areas, two baby swings, two slides, a zip line, a rest area and a washroom, plus trails for walking and biking. Clean and well maintained.
spots.rainbowplayland: A park with a playground for all ages, monkey bars, diggers and a truck climbing structure, a spray park, shade, picnic shelters, clean washrooms and EV charging. Shelters can be reserved.
spots.salishpark: A downtown pond park with geese, ducks, koi and loons and a fountain, handy for a quick lunch with the kids. Don't feed the wild animals.
spots.leppfarmmarket: A big farm market with fresh produce, a deli and bakery, delicious ice cream with fruit flavours, a corn dog and a fully loaded corn cob. Friendly, with a family vibe and higher prices.
spots.myrtlepark: A great park with a playground, swings, a splash park, a little river, bathrooms, trails and a baseball field. Parents sit between the splash park and the playground to watch toddlers.
spots.mcdonaldbeachpark: A Fraser River park with views of the North Shore mountains, lots of sand, a boat launch, an off-leash area, a big field for frisbee and a beach walk at low tide. Plenty of parking.
spots.macleanpark: A full-block park with a huge splash pad, a new-looking playground, a big lawn, shade trees and washrooms, with a good cafe and grocery store on the north side. Street parking is 2 hours.
spots.cloverdaleathleticparksp: A big park with a spray park, playgrounds for toddlers and older kids, huge soccer fields and washrooms, with lots of parking. The washrooms are a walk from the playground.
spots.beachgrovepark: A flat trail along the Boundary Bay dyke with views, birds and a beach with miles of sand at low tide. Pets stay on leash, and there are no restrooms.
spots.nicholaspark: A hidden gem with a playground, splash area, picnic area and washrooms, tennis courts and easy free street parking. There's no shelter, so bring your own on hot days.
spots.mapleridgeleisurecentre: A clean leisure centre with a pool, friendly staff, swim lessons with caring instructors and baby swims. Parking is paid.
spots.newwestminsterfamilyplac: A warm, welcoming drop-in space for young children and parents with a great selection of toys, staff who sanitize everything daily and workshops and programs, including Circle of Security.
spots.chilliwackmuseum: A quality museum with changing exhibits, a kids' craft room, a hall upstairs and well-kept grounds. It's a great school field trip.
spots.milllakepark: Abbotsford's main park, with a paved loop around the lake of about 45 minutes, three kids' play areas, a water park, boardwalks, benches, picnic tables and restrooms. Lots of ducks and geese.
spots.eldonpark: A toddler-friendly park with rubber matting, a spray park, baby swings, a field and a scooter area, plus tennis courts. Busy, with not much shade and limited parking.
spots.gameongo: An indoor game venue with laser, jump and hide-and-seek challenges that burn lots of calories. Fun for families and parties, with free admission on your birthday.
spots.renememorialpark: A lovely local park with a water spray area, a new play area with separate toddler and school-age slides and swings, basketball and a big field. Washrooms are close by and Tim Hortons is nearby.
spots.rainbowpark: A downtown park with a unique wood and plastic playground, a swirly slide, a ground trampoline, a net bridge, a spray pad, a disc swing and a coffee shop. Fun for toddlers up to older kids, and the new slide is fast.
spots.sunnysideacresurbanfores: A serene urban forest of 140 hectares with multiple trails, a stream and a map at the parking lot. Toddlers enjoy exploring, and there's good parking but no washroom.
spots.brandrithpark: A park with baseball fields, tennis courts, a playground, an exercise play ground, clean accessible washrooms and green grass, next to a school.
spots.linwoodpark: A park with a tots section for ages 1.5 to 3, a bigger structure, a zip line and a swing-style accessible zip line, disc swings and an off-leash dog park. Very clean, with little shade.
spots.towncentreparkcommunityc: A community centre by the lake with free play areas, a baby and toy program, Friday family nights, a dessert cafe and warm staff who are great with kids.
spots.albioncommunitycentreacc: A spacious, clean, modern centre with a nice collection of toys and train parts and tables for little kids to play. It hosts craft fairs and markets.
spots.hoperiverkinsmenpark: A peaceful, clean little park with big old trees and lots of shade, where you can watch salmon return upstream.
spots.abbotsfordexhibitionpark: A big park with a walking track, a path all the way around, a playground, sports fields and a flea market on Sundays, plus fireworks on Canada Day and events through the year.
spots.murdofrazerpark: A park with a duck pond with turtles and otters, a creek, a well-equipped playground, free tennis courts and pitch and putt. A short forest walk leads to the Virgin River cabin.
spots.westcoastminiputt: An indoor mini golf with challenging holes, a glow-in-the-dark back nine under black lights and prizes. Great for kids and families. Book online, and it's too dark for some seniors.
spots.burnabylakenaturehouse: A quiet place to feed ducks and go for a flat walk around the lake with little ones, through forest with great birdwatching and sunsets. Check when the Nature House is open.
spots.vancouvermaritimemuseum: A museum where kids can board the restored St. Roch RCMP ship and use a dress-up and play area. Washrooms and a changing table, and it's about 90 minutes to 2 hours.
spots.serpentinefen: A flat, easy trail along the Serpentine River with birds, ducks, blackberries to snack on and views of Mount Baker. Bring bug spray in the evening.
spots.chalmerspark: A peaceful community park with a colourful, safe, well-maintained playground, mature shade trees and wide-open grass areas.
spots.mcleodathleticpark: A park with a playground, picnic tables, a fantastic track and field facility and plane-watching, and it hosts events like Langley Rib Fest.
spots.mundyparktotlot: One of the most advanced playgrounds, with a part for 1-year-olds and a more challenging part for ages 4 and up, shaded areas, a misting station, picnic shelters and trails to a lake. Kids of 5 and 9 both love it.
spots.laitypumpkinpatchnorth: A pumpkin patch with a barn full of farm animals, two pumpkin patches, a tractor-led wagon ride, a fantasy forest, obstacle courses and a cafe. You can easily spend half a day chasing a toddler.
spots.fairfieldpark: A park with baseball fields, a walking track, a lovely playground, shady areas, small ponds with wildlife, an off-leash dog area, washrooms and food trucks at events.
spots.glenvalleyregionalpaabb: A quiet riverside park with views of the North Shore mountains, a walk, boats, a washroom, dog bags and a spot for a family barbeque. Tables and parking are limited, and it closes at 10pm.
spots.kingsmillwalkpark: A popular park with great views of downtown Vancouver and the harbour, a beach volleyball court, a fenced dog area by the beach and porta potties. Parking is limited.
spots.playgroundmcarthurglende: A covered, fenced outdoor playground with soft ground for kids about 4 to 12, benches for parents, free parking and washrooms nearby. Planes fly low overhead, and it's a great break from shopping.
spots.kensingtonparkoutdoorpoo: An outdoor pool that stays open all year, with a diving board, swimming lessons with patient instructors and a great community. Hours change, so check first.
spots.pandorapark: A diverse neighbourhood park with old trees, a playground, a spray park, tennis and basketball courts and a fenced dog area. Parents say it's full of friendly kids and families.
spots.sunnysideplayground: A park with two playgrounds, a free outdoor pool in summer, softball diamonds, tennis courts, a basketball court and lots of parking. Parking fills up during tournaments, and there are no water fountains or washrooms.
spots.beachgrovebeach: A quiet beach spot for kayaks and paddleboards and sunset views, with a few parking spots. Great for a bike break.
spots.braeislandregionalpark: An island park near Fort Langley with a 2.4 km one-way forest trail, Fraser River viewpoints and beaches, free parking, clean washrooms and a lookout.
spots.lowknolllookout: An easy 4 to 5 km hike that kids of 6 and 8 enjoyed in about 3 hours, with a view at the end. A good view-to-effort ratio, and the way down can be slippery.
spots.meadowsfamilyfarmltd: A farm where kids run around, with gentle, sweet animals. Bring a little food to feed them, and a membership is great if you live close.
spots.yarrowpioneerpark: A family park with a playground, a skate park, a water fountain, washrooms, benches, big shade trees and a covered picnic area with 6 tables that you book with the city. It suits ages 2 to 4 best, and hosts a Festival of Lights with a trolley ride.
spots.exitabbotsford: An escape room venue with friendly staff and pop-culture rooms, great for family fun and kids' birthday parties where kids are enthralled by the puzzle. Don't be afraid to ring the bell for a hint.
spots.mosquitocreekpark: A wide gravel creek trail with water access to cool off and fall colours, mostly loved by dogs and walkers. It's a gradual 5 km with a climb if you go all the way.
spots.lansdownecentre: An easy-to-navigate Richmond mall with lots of Asian stores, a huge Chinese supermarket, a food court, family-friendly games and drinks, live music at times and plenty of parking.
spots.mcgillpark: A little north Burnaby park with a sand pit with an excavator toy, a playground for toddlers through elementary, a wading pool, an undercover picnic area and a great sledding hill. No washrooms, and there are wildlife signs.
spots.roundhousecommunityartsr: A lively community centre built with natural wooden beams and big windows, with gyms, snack tables, a courtyard, workshops, events for all ages and a concert hall.
spots.littlecampbellriverh: A volunteer-run salmon hatchery with friendly, knowledgeable volunteers, hatching ponds and a roughly 20-minute trail. Easy-to-read signs teach kids about plants and the area's history.
spots.mountainviewpark: A small park with a great lawn, a kids' playground, free parking and a little forest with fairy-tale characters on display.
spots.walnutgrovecommunitypark: A park with two playgrounds for young and older kids, a spray park, a covered picnic shelter, baseball and soccer fields, washrooms and a quiet walking trail. Parking fills up on weekends with sports.
spots.coquitlamcentre: A big, clean, bright mall with a kids' play area, a food court, outdoor seating and a wide mix of stores. Parking is easy on the upper deck.
spots.northshorebike: An indoor bike park with a pump track, jumps, a children's area and a half pipe being built. Parents say the staff are epic, and an all-day price with rental helmets is affordable. Bring snacks.
spots.kinsmenpark: A park with a little kids' play set with baby swings, a tire swing, a basketball court, tennis courts, lots of benches and a paved walkway all the way around. Watch for broken glass near the tables.
spots.grantpark: A park with a playground with unique structures for all ages, shade, picnic tables, washrooms and lots of parking. It's beside Highway 1, so it's loud, and it's good for a baby's birthday party.
spots.grandboulevardpark: A long, paved garden boulevard from 19th to 13th Street with benches, picnic tables, an outdoor big chess set, lit evening walking and a 30-minute loop.
spots.papaworldkidsindoorplayg: A new, very clean indoor playground with all new equipment, friendly attentive staff and two big rooms for food at birthday parties. Parents can actually relax.
spots.kushiropark: A peaceful hilltop park with beautiful views of the mountains and the city at sunset, unique wooden sculptures, floral arrangements and an open green space for a family picnic.
spots.stanleyparkplayground: A playground next to Second Beach with slides, enough swings for small kids and toddlers, big fields, food trucks, movies in the park and a public pool nearby. It has little shade.
spots.claytoncommunitycentre: A brand-new, welcoming community centre, North America's first Passive House certified centre, with lots of parking, a gym, a library on the second floor and a Clayton night market.
spots.bellpark: A neighbourhood ball park with a small playground, a public washroom and two baseball diamonds, one for small kids. Pick up after your dogs.
spots.citypark: A park with a dinosaur-themed playground, a water spray park, an outdoor pool, three covered picnic shelters you can reserve (with power outlets and charging stations), benches and washrooms. Free parking.
spots.poiriersportleisurecompl: A big Coquitlam complex with ice skating and lacrosse rinks, a pool and hot tubs that are family friendly, and kids' skating lessons with kind coaches.
spots.lowerfallstrail: An easy, wide gravel trail, about 2.5 km from the parking lot to the lower falls, suitable for all ages with almost no elevation. It gets crowded on weekends, so keep kids safe by the falls.
spots.websterpark: A park with bathrooms, a drink fountain, a running trail, a kids' playground, a small skate park with scooter kids, new fitness equipment and a large grass area.
spots.thereachgallerymuseum: A quiet art gallery and museum with interactive exhibits, a history section about Abbotsford at the back, and friendly volunteers. Entry is by donation.
spots.bridgmanpark: A fenced, shaded play structure with mini slides and a basket swing that suits a 9-month-old, a dog park, a picnic area, washrooms and a creek with river access.
spots.lavenderland: A lavender farm with photo spots, a little play area for kids, workshops, a shop with lavender items and a walking path. It's smaller than some expect, and mid-June is when it's in bloom.
spots.museumofarchaeologyethno: A small SFU museum with carvings, sculptures and a soil layers wall kids like. It takes about 30 minutes, and you need to find your way inside the building.
spots.falsecreekcommunitycentr: A small community centre on Granville Island with a big gym, a pottery room, welcoming bathrooms, before- and after-school care and a water park right behind it. Parking is tough.
spots.fraserheightsrecreationc: A clean recreation centre with a gym, fitness classes, friendly staff and plenty of parking.
spots.corydrivepark: A quiet, well-maintained little neighbourhood playground for little tots, with trails nearby. It has limited parking, and the area could use more lights.
spots.willowbrookmall: Langley's biggest mall with a good food court, lots of space, a clean, cool, uncrowded feel and most major retailers, plus an acai bowl spot near the north entrance.
spots.mellowclaystudio: A cosy pottery studio where the patient teacher guides beginners, including kids. A parent took a 10-year-old and both had a great time.
spots.mygymchildrensfitnesscen: A kids' fitness centre with classes, friendly enthusiastic staff and well-priced birthday parties with games and activities for varying ages.
spots.sardispark: A pond with an easy flat loop, geese, ducks and turtles, two small playgrounds including a new semi-covered one, a washroom, an adult outdoor gym and benches.
spots.clearbrookpark: A park with many trails around the fields and through the forest, a baseball diamond, a grass soccer field, an off-leash dog area and outhouses along the way.
spots.moodyvillepark: A kids' park for all ages with swings, zip lines, climbing structures, a sand and water digging area, a really long slide, a mini trampoline and a concrete pump track nearby. Public washrooms, and it's busy.
spots.hamiltoncommunitycentre: A friendly little community centre with great programs for kids and patient, kind staff.
spots.kidoodlesartstudio: A cheerful art studio for kids' birthday parties, such as doll painting, where kids concentrate happily and parents can do a quick shop at nearby T&T.
spots.beaconsfieldparkplaygrou: A refreshed playground with soft foamy ground, a big sand pit, two trampolines, a rope climbing structure, logs, spinners and swings, next to a community garden, a field and washrooms. Some structures are high for little ones.
spots.donchristianrecreationce: A recreation centre with a park with a hockey area, volleyball and basketball nets and fields, bouncy castle birthday parties and kind after-school care staff.
spots.douglasjhusbanddiscovery: A free local museum with quality displays, family-friendly community events and a Friday baby and me museum program. Park at the visitor spot.
spots.academyfarms: A farm with a family-friendly tour, bison and water buffalo, a small farm shop with buffalo meat, yogurt, cheese and fresh vegetables, and knowledgeable staff. Kids loved it, and the buffalo milk sells out fast.
spots.rochesteradventurepark: A big park with a zip line, climbing logs, nets and ladders, a long windy tunnel slide, a tot play area, a splash park, a sand area, a playing field and washrooms. Plenty for all ages.
spots.spireanaturetrail: A short (under 1 km), flat, easy forest trail in Golden Ears with mossy trees, ferns and accessible parking, suitable for children and seniors. Shady for a rainy day, and magical in autumn.
spots.greatblueheronnaturerese: A nature reserve with a great blue heron colony, many pathways, benches, viewing blinds, picnic areas, washrooms and a small gift shop with taxidermy. Free admission, with bullfrogs, salmon and waterfowl to spot.
spots.playabbyabbotsford: An indoor playground with two play areas, one for under 5s and one for older kids. Socks are required, and Tim Hortons is in the same parking lot. Parents like it for birthdays and burning off energy.
spots.thepolygongallery: A lovely North Vancouver gallery with admission by donation, interesting photo exhibits and a good photography bookstore. A visit takes about 40 minutes.
spots.stevestoncommunitycentre: A cosy, compact community centre with a gym, a swimming pool, parks, a library and a friendly, welcoming vibe.
spots.lewarnepark: A park beside a school with an outdoor pool with a kids' pool in summer, a basketball court and a grassy area.
spots.creeksidecommunityrecrea: A modern community centre with a big open gym with natural light, a fitness centre, a lounge, childcare, water programs and dragon boat training. Parking is hard to find, and the underground lot is easier.
spots.newtonrecreationcentre: A recreation centre with a wave pool with two large slides and a kids' play area, which kids still enjoy, plus helpful staff and classes.
spots.southdeltarecreationcent: A local community centre with a hockey rink, curling rink, two gyms, a pottery club, clean washrooms, a lacrosse rink, skateboard parks and EV charging, with tons of parking.
spots.krauseberryfarms: A u-pick berry farm with strawberries, raspberries and blueberries, and you can eat as you pick. Waffles with berries including gluten-free and vegan options, live acoustic music and a family-day-out feel.
spots.mundyparkpool: An outdoor pool with several pools (warm and cool), a lazy river, water jets, a spray park for toddlers, a hot tub, a big lawn with picnic tables and a good concession. Reserve online, since it gets crowded, and 3 hours does just fine.
spots.therockwallclimbinggym: A family-run climbing gym that parents call a great family activity, with encouraging staff and a friendly atmosphere. Kids love the field trips.
spots.klaassenfarms: A huge blueberry farm with lots of aisles to pick, an awesome playground with a big bouncy trampoline, a sand pit, a playhouse, mini golf and goats, plus ice cream at the farm store and mountain views.
spots.jubileepark: A small downtown Abbotsford park with a recently redone children's play area, new washrooms, a water fountain, a field, a farmers market and music in July.
spots.treetopsadventure: A walk high among towering evergreens on a series of smaller suspension bridges that are more stable than the main Capilano bridge, with views and fairytale lights.
spots.seaislandcommunitycentre: A small, friendly community centre in Burkeville with a wonderful preschool, a clean hall for events and yoga and Pilates classes.
spots.clawzonearcade: A bright, new, clean claw machine arcade with about 50 machines, anime plushies and stationery prizes, friendly staff and different difficulty levels. Kids and parents stay longer than planned.
spots.mountpleasantcommunityce: A community centre with a library attached, friendly staff, a gym and programs. Underground parking costs over $7 an hour.
spots.cloverdalerecreationcent: A new, clean recreation centre with spacious, sunlit gyms, wood beam architecture, lots of parking and well-run birthday parties including art-themed ones. The indoor basketball court is helpful on rainy days.
spots.owlrehab: A raptor rehabilitation centre that treats over 1,000 raptors a year, where you can see owls and other birds of prey up close. Knowledgeable, passionate staff, with lots of parking.
spots.gvmezosoic: A huge zoo and Jurassic-style dinosaur park with giraffes, a kangaroo keeper, a tourist train and well-maintained dinosaurs with movement and sound. Bring your own bike or scooter, since it's big.
spots.coquitlampubliclibrarypo: A busy library with a generous kids' space, a train set, tablets, a child-height water fountain, baby story times on some Sundays and a large selection of titles.
spots.firefighterspark: A well-kept playground with a play fire truck, a pump track, a bike track, a sand area with a water spout, a half basketball court, a skateboard ramp and a trail. No shade, so bring a tent. Fire trucks drive in next door often.
spots.edmondspark: A big city park with an extensive playground, an entertaining spray park, lots of picnic tables and grass, tennis, pickleball and table tennis, paths for little ones on bikes and scooters, and a community centre with washrooms nearby. Busy on summer weekends.
spots.sumodino: A busy claw-machine and play centre at Lansdowne Centre that kids love, with patient staff and well-set-up birthday parties with a plushie photo wall.
spots.watermania: A big Richmond aquatic centre with a wave pool with a kids' play structure and small waterslides, a lane pool with diving boards and two large water slides. Call ahead, since swim meets can limit the deep end.
spots.richmondcentre: A clean, well-kept mall with a big food court, high ceilings, free parking, an outdoor plaza and a kids' play section outside Sport Chek.
spots.centralcity: A big arcade fun park with bowling, roller skating, mini golf and carnival-style games, reasonably priced with free parking in the designated area. Parents say it's a hit with 4-year-olds up to bigger kids, with birthday parties.
spots.museumsurrey: A free local history museum with a playroom, a birthday party room and a hockey gallery where kids can try playing hockey. Events like an Easter Bunny visit, and a donation is welcome.
spots.guildford: A large Surrey mall with lots of shops, a big food court and entertainment, popular with families.
spots.activate: Interactive game rooms with a mega laser room and a play maze, plenty of parking, clean bathrooms and lockers, and friendly staff. Recommended for ages 6 and up, and it can be loud and packed.
spots.aldor: A family farm with lots of friendly animals to pet and feed, a goat parade, baby animals the staff help kids hold and a bakery. Parents say it's worth the admission, and it's great for birthday parties.
spots.penzer: An action park with a bike park, skate park, climbing, balancing, parkour, an obstacle course, basketball, a hockey area, parking and a washroom. The main climbing area is for 5 and up, with a smaller one for younger kids.
spots.shipyards: A waterfront plaza with a pier, shops, restaurants, a skate zone, lots of seating, night markets and pop-ups in summer, and harbour views. Good for a stroll or a short outing with the kids.
spots.lonsdalequay: A market by the SeaBus terminal with a food hall, a third-floor walkway with views, restaurants and a great skyline view across the harbour.
spots.richmondcountryfarms: A clean farm market with fresh produce, local BC products and flowers, a nursery and farm animals to see. Kids enjoy it, and there's a big parking lot.
spots.portkells: A cute, less busy pumpkin patch with small activities for little ones, a food truck, face painting, a tree maze, farm animals to feed and a play area, at a garden nursery.
spots.maplewoodfarm: A small, peaceful hobby farm with horses, cows, ducks, chickens and other animals, where you can buy food to feed some of them. Great for toddlers, with a picnic spot.
spots.gobananas: An indoor play centre with climbing, sliding and running, an arcade, clean play areas and friendly staff. A good value pass lets kids use all the play areas, and it's great for birthdays.
spots.clipnclimb: Colourful climbing walls with auto-belays where kids climb as high as they like, with easy and challenging climbs and party rooms. Mostly good for ages 6 and up, with one-hour climbing slots.
spots.vancouverpubliclibraryce: A striking 9-floor central library with a rooftop garden on the ninth floor, a children's section, a historical section, a coffee shop and musical programs.
spots.crescentbeach: A calm beach with shallow swimming areas, sunsets, a long seaside path, and low-tide walks. Good for kids and families, with nearby gelato, fish and chips.
spots.guildfordrecreationcentr: A family-friendly, wheelchair-accessible pool with a kids' pool, leisure pool, hot tub and sauna, free events, a coffee shop and lots of camps for children.
spots.capilanoriverhatchery: A free salmon hatchery where kids can see salmon swim up a man-made fishway through glass, with picnic tables, trails and viewing panels. Late October to November is the best time, and parking is limited.
spots.surreysportleisurecomple: A clean, well-maintained aquatic complex with waterslides, a lazy river, a hot tub and a kids' pool, great for families.
spots.sungodrecreationcentre: A local recreation centre with a pool next to a rink and a sauna.
spots.emmaleafarms: A clean, well-kept farm with u-pick strawberries and blueberries, a farm market and an ice cream shack. The berries are sweet and good-sized, and the farm is open later on weekends.
spots.bonsorrecreationcomplex: A big complex with a swimming pool, a gym, a banquet hall, multi-purpose rooms, a snack bar, classes and kids' activities. Swim lessons get great reviews.
spots.coalharbourcommunitycent: A modern community centre with programs for all ages, before- and after-school care, a daycare, a big underground parking lot and a waterfront view.
spots.surreyartgallerysurreyci: A beautiful arts centre in a park with art, theatre shows, kids' camps in pottery, drawing and drama, an outdoor area, a cafe and lots of parking.
spots.fleetwoodcommunitycentre: A clean, bright community centre with a library, a gym, camps and an outdoor area for kids, in a beautiful neighbourhood.
spots.tonglouiefamilyymca: A clean, modern family YMCA with a pool, hot tub, steam room, a daycare and programs for kids.
spots.douglasparkcommunitycent: A small, welcoming community centre with a drop-in playgroup for babies and toddlers and what one parent calls perhaps the best playground in Vancouver.
spots.burnabypubliclibrarybobp: A busy community library with friendly staff, a renovated space and lots of kids around.
spots.victoriapark: A pretty park in the middle of North Vancouver with flowers in spring, a cenotaph, chestnuts in fall and a picnic area, good for a walk any time of year.
spots.kerrisdalecommunitycentr: A community centre with a swimming pool, arts and crafts, indoor activities that kids love and polite, helpful staff. Parking is becoming paid.
spots.southarmcommunitycentre: A modern, spacious Richmond community centre with an arena, recreation programs, summer camps and well-kept outdoor spaces.
spots.thompsoncommunitycentre: A bright community centre with child and youth programs, a very well-kept playground, a skate area and a spot to sit and work.
spots.kensingtonpark: A park with soccer and baseball fields, a running track, tennis courts, a small creek and an easy pitch and putt course, with cherry blossoms in spring and fall colours.
spots.capitolhillreservoirpark: A hilltop viewpoint with stunning views of the North Shore and Vancouver, great for an evening picnic and sunsets. It's not a proper park, parking is tricky, and you should bring food and drinks.
spots.byrnecreekravinepark: A forest-feeling ravine walk of about 3 km along a creek near Edmonds Station, with a children's playground with slides, swings, a seesaw and a wading pool, public restrooms, a picnic area and courts.
spots.wcblairrecreationcentre: A recreation centre with a pool with a decent shallow end and water tables for little ones, a hot tub, saunas, cheap kid activities and lifeguards who are great with kids.
spots.hiknolldrivingrangeminig: A beautiful family-owned mini golf course with immaculate gardens and turf, walk-in play at about $16 per person and a driving range. There's an hour limit for 18 holes.
spots.wildbirdtrustofbc: A flat 30-minute trail with ponds, wildflowers, great songbird variety, tame spotted towhees and views of Burrard Inlet. Bring binoculars.
spots.karenmagnussencommunityr: A community centre with a wave pool made for children, a leisure area, two ice rinks with public sessions, a fitness area and a great pool and rink schedule for elementary kids.
spots.cliffwalk: A thrilling narrow walkway hugging granite cliffs with glass sections and views of the Capilano River far below, with a restaurant and grill. BC residents can get a one-time ticket that gives access for a year.
spots.renfrewparkcommunitycent: A smaller community centre with a decent-size pool, sauna, hot tub, a library next door, a fitness area and friendly staff.
spots.richmondpubliclibrarybri: A bright, spacious, two-floor library with a kids' reading and movie area, a Summer Reading Club, a digital makerspace, 3D printing and free covered parking.
spots.cloverdalearena: A clean, well-kept rink for learning to skate with family, and a beautifully decorated Winter Ice Palace in the holidays. A Sunday flea market is held here.
spots.northsurreysporticecompl: A new facility with three ice rinks, small-group skating classes, a seating area with heaters for parents, a concession counter, a gym and climbing boulders.
spots.lowerseymourconservation: A reserve with hiking and biking trails, an easy 30-minute loop at Rice Lake, a smooth trail to the dam and a washroom. Parking is limited, so come early.
spots.uufamilyfarm: A farm that parents say is a safe space for toddlers to explore, where the kids had a blast with the animals.
spots.aldergrovecommunitycentr: A family favourite with three waterslides, a spray park, a lazy river, a wave pool, diving boards, a hot tub, an ice rink and a sophisticated children's playground. Clean and well run, with friendly staff.
spots.cambiecommunitycentre: A spacious, welcoming community centre with gyms, a fitness centre, a dance studio, an Easter egg hunt and ample parking.
spots.projectclimbingcloverdal: A beginner-friendly bouldering gym with lots of V0 and V0+ climbs good for kids, a friendly community and staff who explain without overwhelming. Kids of 7 to 9 were tired and happy.
spots.killarneypool: A pool with a lazy river, a good slide, warm ozone-treated water and a wall of windows with great views. Family swim is popular.
spots.northvancouvercitylibrar: A modern glass library with a welcoming children's floor, a garden and play area, quiet study spaces, and a wide collection of books, movies and games.
spots.ladnerleisurecentre: A versatile community centre with an ice rink, a pool, a gym, fitness classes and a Blenz coffee. Staff are fun and helpful, and kids swim here.
spots.surreylibrariesnewtonbra: A spacious library with a quiet room, many seats, parking and welcoming staff. Story time is a favourite.
spots.newbrightonpool: One of the few Vancouver outdoor pools, open from May long weekend to Labour Day, with a lovely view and a small playground on a big lawn. Book ahead because it gets busy, and bring snacks.
spots.citycentrecommunitycentr: A spacious, modern Richmond community centre with a pool and lots of classes, including hip hop and STEAM classes for kids.
spots.rondrisofarmsgeneralstor: A farm with a pumpkin patch and general store with eggs, fruit and vegetables, cows and chickens in the barn, and more to do than just pick pumpkins. Pet-friendly, with a calmer feel than busier patches.
spots.seymourcreekgolfcentre: A mini putt and driving range that's affordable, with a mini golf course ($8) and a bucket of balls, mostly adult-oriented. The facility is showing its age.
spots.surreylibrariesguildford: A homey library attached to the rec centre, with a good kids' section, helpful staff, children's programs and audio and video collections.
